title: Semantic Atlas
concept: An editorial field atlas gives engineering knowledge a readable geography: types occupy bounded terrain, an instance is a precise survey mark, named relations become directed routes, and applicability stops at an explicit human review frontier. The five phases change scale and composition from an archipelago to a type survey, an entry-dependent terrain map, a review crossing, and a folded reference atlas. All diagram data is illustrative, not performed engineering.
metaphor: A cartographic atlas with contour lines, survey diamonds, route arrows, a review river, and a folded map.
choreography: Five adjoining territories establish distinct knowledge types; a survey baseline quietly binds the collection.
The atlas zooms into the Pump type and its Pump A instance, then traces the named applies to relation from Head balance.
Equipment, method, or evidence changes the highlighted terrain, route geometry, relation caption, and complete statement while keeping source facts fixed.
A dashed proposed applicability route encounters the human review frontier; a finite stamp reveal leaves the Pending state readable.
The atlas folds into a portable reference preserving type, instance, method, evidence, relation, and the unresolved applicability status.
interaction: The supplied equipment/method/evidence choice selects a contextual reading: Head balance applies to Pump A; Head balance requires input Flow condition; or Head balance is supported by Reference excerpt. These are proposed illustrative relations, not proof of applicability. The host rerenders the chosen state directly.
contributions: Nested cartographic boundaries and survey diamonds distinguish type membership from a concrete instance without a generic hub graph.
A pure render function exposes three meaningful contextual routes with stable underlying facts and authored English/Korean strings.
A reusable review-frontier visual separates a named connection from verified applicability; finite animation obeys pause and reduced-motion settings.
limitations: Static illustrative ontology only. No engineering calculation, source verification, applicability assessment, or human approval has been performed. The diagram intentionally shows a small curated subset; it is not a general graph layout engine. Browser and device rendering are left to the shared host validation.
